extracted.intended_audience: authors, reviewers, and action editors using the JMLR online submission/review system
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural guidance and requirements for submitting manuscripts, responding to review requests, submitting reviews, and managing manuscripts in the Journal of Machine Learning Research online system. Covers file formats, revision policy, reviewer handling, database upkeep, and related operational rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript file format
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts should be submitted in PDF format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your file is particularly large (due to images, for instance), compress it and submit a compressed file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple files and visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: You may submit multiple files on the submission page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replies to prior reviews can be submitted this way. For each additional document, you may select whether reviewers can see it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision submission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit a revised manuscript only if the action editor has specifically encouraged you to submit a revised manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If in doubt, consult the action editor immediately after receiving your reviews. Use the manuscript listing to submit your revision; it will automatically be linked as a revision of the previous manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-submission inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: JMLR does not respond to pre-submission inquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you believe your manuscript is in-scope for the journal, please submit it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of the journal
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should confirm whether a paper is within the journal's scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the journal scope page for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action editor assignment timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: An Action Editor will be assigned to a submission no later than one month after submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address inquiries about the status of a paper under review to the Action Editor in charge of your paper (the AE's name appears in the submission system once assigned).

rubrics_metrics.name: How to submit a review (procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: To submit a review, go to the manuscript listing, select the manuscript, and click 'submit review'. Provide a recommendation and upload a review file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can also enter a 'private comments' file to be seen only by the editor. Press 'submit' to complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review file formats and anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: Review files can be in any commonly readable format, but JMLR heavily advises against Microsoft Word format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MS Word usually contains identifying information hidden in the file and therefore violates the anonymity of the review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to reviewer invitations without an account
rubrics_metrics.description: If you received an e-mail requesting you review a manuscript but do not have an account, use the long URL in the e-mail to respond without creating an account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you want an account so all your reviews are under one interface, register using the same e-mail address to which the request was sent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to reviewer invitations with an account
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have an account, log in, select 'Manuscript Listing' then 'Reviewer', locate the manuscript, and enter your response (yes/no) under the reply section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entering your response on the website prevents automated reminder emails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling reminders after declining a review
rubrics_metrics.description: If you declined a review by e-mail but did not record that response on the website, you may continue to receive reminders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options: (1) go to the web site and select 'yes' or 'no' to indicate willingness to review; (2) send another e-mail to the action editor asking them to update the site; (3) e-mail the managing editor to update the database.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updating the database when you requested a reviewer outside the system
rubrics_metrics.description: If you already requested a reviewer via e-mail (outside of the system), update the online database to reflect this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request the reviewer as normal but select 'Request, do not send e-mail.' Then return to the manuscript listing, select 'show' under reviews and 'yes' under 'force reply' for that reviewer so the database reflects the correct information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entering e-mailed reviews into the system
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reviewer sent a review via e-mail and did not enter it into the system, the Action Editor should enter the review manually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Go to the manuscript's listing and select 'submit review' next to the reviewer's name; you can submit the review on the reviewer's behalf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entering decisions into the system
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions sent to authors by e-mail must still be entered into the online system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After entering the decision, you will reach a page to send the authors an e-mail; if you have already e-mailed them, select 'do not send e-mail' at the bottom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extending reviewer due dates
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reviewer agreed to do the review but needs extra time, edit the due date for that reviewer in the manuscript listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Otherwise the reviewer will receive automated reminder e-mails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixing incorrect or stale reminder e-mails
rubrics_metrics.description: If you receive an e-mail reminder about a manuscript that has already been handled, update the system or contact the managing editor to correct the database.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have the missing information outside the system, enter it; otherwise contact the managing editor (managing@jmlr.org) to have the database fixed. Duplicate requests may cause lingering reminders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viewing manuscript listings and filters
rubrics_metrics.description: To see your manuscripts, select 'manuscript listing' and choose the correct 'connection' (author, reviewer, or action editor) and appropriate filters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For 'author' and 'reviewer' the default filter is 'all'. If you don't see the manuscript tag you want, set 'manuscript status' filter to 'all' and select 'refilter', or type the tag into the find box. If multiple tags appear, select the tag for the manuscript you want to view details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of browser 'back' button and page freshness
rubrics_metrics.description: The browser 'back' button mostly works, but avoid resubmitting a form you just submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most browsers warn about re-submitting forms. You may need to prompt your browser to reload if information is out-of-date. The site uses no cookies or other tracking mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Password reset procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have forgotten your password, use the reset page and enter your e-mail address to receive your username and a new password by e-mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If password reset does not work, e-mail the managing editor (managing@jmlr.org).
